status_summary: On 2025-03-27 HHS announced a restructuring that would combine OASH with HRSA, SAMHSA, ATSDR and NIOSH into a new Administration for a Healthy America and consolidate redundant units; the release does not mention the Surgeon General or the Commissioned Corps. As of August 2025 Congress had not created or funded the new agency and a federal court had temporarily blocked parts of the reorganization, and the House Appropriations Committee approved its FY 2027 Labor-HHS-Education bill 34 to 28 on 2026-06-09; that this bill again does not create or fund the new agency is an unverified lead from advocacy-group summaries, since the committee release and a CRS report do not address it. title: Combine the Assistant Secretary for Health and Surgeon General into one four-star post
uncertainties: The HHS release of 2025-03-27 (titled HHS Announces Transformation to Make America Healthy Again) was re-read in review: it folds OASH, HRSA, SAMHSA, ATSDR and NIOSH into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America and does not mention the Surgeon General or the Commissioned Corps. A law-firm summary of the FY 2027 budget (2026-04) shows the consolidation proposed again. A news report of 2026-04-10, read in review, states that a District of Rhode Island judge denied HHS's motion to dismiss on 2026-04-07 in the suit by 19 states and the District of Columbia over the restructuring, after an earlier preliminary injunction and a denied stay request; the court order and docket were not opened (courtlistener.com refuses automated fetches) and the suit concerns the reorganization, not the Surgeon General merger. A Federal Register API search in review for Surgeon General, Assistant Secretary for Health and reorganization since 2025-01-20 returned one unrelated standards of conduct rule; no statement of organization merging the posts was found. The House committee approval of 2026-06-09 (34 to 28) and the reporting of the bill on 2026-06-11 as H.R. 9260 (H.Rept. 119-696) are confirmed by the committee release and CRS report R49344, neither of which mentions the Administration for a Healthy America; the statement that the bill does not create or fund it comes only from summaries by the National Council of Urban Indian Health and the Addiction Policy Forum, both advocacy groups, and is an unverified lead at low confidence; the bill text and committee report were not read. A Surgeon General nomination is an appointment to the existing post, not a merger. The record rests largely on absence of an action; the Unified Agenda, Congress and news checks of a full systematic review were not run.
